essence: A trading city where merchants of seven nations meet at every solstice and equinox to exchange not only wares but, around the night fires, memories, so that each traveller carries home stories that have quietly become someone else's.
textDetails: It is reached by travelling eighty miles into the north-west wind.
Merchants of seven nations gather there at every solstice and every equinox, so the fair happens four times a year.
A boat arrives laden with ginger and cotton and sails again with its hold full of pistachio nuts and poppy seeds.
A caravan unloads sacks of nutmeg and raisins and is already packing its saddlebags with bolts of golden muslin for the return.
Traders come up rivers and across deserts to reach it.

The wares are no different from those of any bazaar inside or outside the Great Khan's empire: spread on the same yellow mats, shaded by the same awnings against the flies, sold with the same dishonest discounts.
What really draws people is the night, when fires burn all around the market.
Listeners sit on sacks or barrels or stretch out on piles of carpets.
One man says a single word and each of the others tells his own tale of it; the words given are wolf, sister, hidden treasure, battle, scabies, lovers.
On the long road home, kept awake by a camel's sway or a junk's rocking, the traveller calls up his memories one by one.
He finds that his wolf has turned into another wolf, his sister into a different sister, his battles into other battles.
Euphemia is named as the city where memory is traded at every solstice and every equinox.
Not in the text: any buildings, walls or streets beyond the market and its fires; the river bank, dunes, nation camps and sky ring in this brief are staging.
visualConcept: A floating island of packed ochre earth that carries both roads of trade: a slow indigo river curving along its west side, with a timber wharf and a moored junk, and wind-combed dunes on its east side, where a camel caravan kneels beside its saddlebags. At the centre lies the market, a grid of yellow mats heaped with goods in spice colours (pale ginger roots, white cotton bales, green pistachios, blue-grey poppy seed, brown nutmeg sacks, dark raisins, bolts of golden muslin) under striped awnings. Around it stand seven camps, one per nation, each with its own colour of tents and banner, and seven fires ring the market, where tiny merchants sit on sacks and barrels or lie on piles of carpets. The conceit becomes visible at night: a speaker at one fire 'says' a word and a luminous constellation-glyph of it rises from his flames (a howling wolf, a sister in a long dress, a chest with a spark inside, two crossed spears, a scatter of red specks for scabies, two lovers in profile), and every other fire answers with its own version of the same glyph, in its nation's colour and in a slightly different drawing. The glyphs drift from fire to fire, trading points as they pass, so a slowly turning carousel of variants of the same few words hangs above the market. Some glyphs leave with the departing caravan and junk and keep rearranging themselves as they shrink into the fog: the wolf that leaves is no longer the wolf that came. Overhead, a thin gold ring tilted like the ecliptic carries four small bead-lamps for the two solstices and two equinoxes, one of them lit, to say that the fair exists only at these hinges of the year. Glyphs are point-and-line figures (8 to 14 points each, additive blending, strong bloom); everything else is low-poly primitives with warm firelit shading.
layout: North = -z, east = +x. Island disc radius 22, top at y=0, 2.5 thick with a crumbling earth underside. Centre: market plaza 12 x 12 with 42 yellow mats (0.9 x 0.6) in 7 rows x 6 columns, 0.5 aisles, a small heap of goods on each; 14 striped awnings (1.6 x 1.2 canopies at y=0.75 on four poles). Ring of 7 fires at radius 9, one every 51.4 degrees (fire 0.3 across, flames 0.45 tall), each with 6 to 8 seated merchants (0.25 tall) on sacks, barrels and carpet stacks. Behind each fire, at radius 11 to 14, its nation's camp: 3 tents (cone, dome or ridge, 0.8 to 1.2 tall) and a 2-unit banner pole in the nation's colour (saffron #e2a93b, madder #a8442f, indigo #34407a, verdigris #3f8f80, plum #6b3f6b, ivory #efe3c6, henna #c0653a). West sector (south-west to north-west): river channel 3 wide on an arc at radius about 16.5, water at y=-0.2, emerging from and vanishing into fog; a timber wharf 6 long on the inner bank with a junk moored (hull 3.2 long, two battened sails 2.4 tall, rust-red), a second junk on a slow arrive-and-depart loop. East sector (north-east to south-east): 6 dunes up to 2.5 high from radius 15 to the rim, a caravan track from the east rim to the market's east aisle, 8 camels (hump 0.38) with saddlebags and 3 drivers. Glyph layer between y=2 and y=7 above the fire ring. Sky ring: thin gold torus radius 18 at y=15, tilted 23.5 degrees, with four bead-lamps at its quarter points.
signatureMotion: 1) Word and answers (night, about every 10 s): one fire flares and its sparks assemble into a word-glyph above it; the six other fires flare in turn 0.6 s apart, each launching its own variant of the same word in its nation's colour; the variants rise on arcs and join a slow orbit above the market (period about 60 s), their points continually re-linking so each slowly becomes a different drawing of the same word. 2) Departure: on a 90 s loop the camels rise and plod east over the dunes (swaying 1.2 s gait) while a junk slips downstream, each carrying one glyph that keeps mutating as it recedes into the fog. 3) Ambient: fire flicker and embers rising into the glyph layer, awnings rippling in the north-west wind, smoke and dust drifting south-east, and a small sun-bead creeping along the sky ring toward the lit equinox lamp.
interactionDescription: Switches from the night fair of memories (default) to the noon fair of goods: the sky brightens to hot white-gold, the fires sink to thin smoke, the glyphs fade out, flies speck the air over the mats, and cargo shuttles in small arcs: ginger and cotton bales off the junk and sacks of pistachios and poppy seed onto it, nutmeg and raisin sacks off the camels and bolts of golden muslin onto them, while merchants haggle on the yellow mats. The goods leave exactly as they came; switching back relights the fires and the stories begin drifting and changing again.
mood: Equinox night just after sunset: a last band of apricot dust on the western horizon under a deep indigo sky with the first stars; seven fires as the main light, warm orange pools on the yellow mats, long flickering shadows, smoke and embers leaning south-east in the north-west wind; dry, warm, murmuring air. Daylight state: high white-gold noon, short hard shadows, dusty haze.
caption: Four times a year, when the sun stands at a solstice or an equinox, seven nations unroll their yellow mats in Euphemia. By day ginger is weighed against pistachios and nutmeg against golden muslin, as in any bazaar. By night, around the fires, one man says a single word, wolf or sister or battle, and everyone answers with a story of his own. The spices travel home unchanged. The memories do not: each traveller leaves with a wolf that was never his.
motto: Spices come home unchanged; memories come home as strangers.
camera: Three-quarter view from the south-south-east, distance about 44 units, elevation about 30 degrees, target slightly above the market centre (0, 1.5, 0): the ring of fires in the lower middle, the glyph carousel above it, wharf and junk at frame left, dunes and caravan at frame right; very slow auto-orbit (about 3 degrees per 10 s).
